mainTopic: The value of the סלע for פדיון הבן (the Torah's original סלע and the rabbinic addition), other biblical coin values, and whether coins made from Temple metal may be used
overview: רבי יוחנן gives a practical way to find the twenty דינרים (five סלעים) owed for פדיון הבן, starting from a worn gold coin worth twenty-five זוזים. The גמרא checks his arithmetic twice. It concludes that you first remove one זוז and then a sixth, which leaves exactly twenty, and it also restates that amount in מתקלי. רבא then proves from a פסוק, the תרגום and a ברייתא that the Torah's original סלע is only three and a third דינרים. A ברייתא says a holy סלע is forty-eight פונדיונין, which is four דינרים. The גמרא answers that this describes the time after the חכמים added a sixth, which the Torah allows (they may add, but never reduce). The story of רב אשי and רב אחא shows that in practice the larger amount of twenty דינרים is paid. רבי חנינא explains how much an unspecified 'silver' is in the Torah, נביאים and כתובים, with עפרון's silver as an exception. Finally, אביי explains that the חכמים considered banning the worn coins of הדריינוס and טריינוס because they contained ירושלים's Temple metal. A פסוק showed that plundered Temple metal loses its holiness.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's method for calculating פדיון הבן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says to take the worn gold coin that sells for twenty-five זוזים, subtract a sixth, and what remains is the amount for פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: the worn-out דינר of הדריינוס and טריינוס, which is sold for twenty-five זוזים — take away a sixth from them, and what is left is for פדיון הבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a practical formula for figuring out how much money a father must give for פדיון הבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires five סלעים, which equals twenty דינרים (זוזים), since a סלע is four דינרים. רבי יוחנן ties this amount to a familiar market coin worth twenty-five זוזים. He says to subtract a sixth from it to reach the target.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption of the firstborn son, done by paying five סלעים to a כהן
Worn-out, rubbed down (a coin that has lost some weight)
זוזים — silver coins, the same as דינרים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
the worn-out dinar of Hadrian and Trajan
phrases.notes: Gold coins named after Roman emperors

phrases.english: which is sold for twenty-five zuz,
take away a sixth from them
and these are for the redemption of the son.
phrases.notes: What's left should come to five סלעים, which is 20 זוזים.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Take the 25-זוז coin, subtract a sixth, and the rest is the amount for פדיון הבן.

steps.title: The math does not come out to twenty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that 25 minus a sixth of 25 leaves 20⅚, which is twenty-one less a sixth, not twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these are twenty-one less a sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks רבי יוחנן's arithmetic and finds that it does not give exactly twenty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sixth of 25 is 4⅙. Subtracting it leaves 20⅚, which is "21 minus one דנקא." That is almost a whole זוז more than the twenty needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A sixth of a זוז (same as a מעה)

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי עֶשְׂרִין וְחַד נְכֵי דַּנְקָא הָוֵי!
phrases.english: These are twenty-one less a sixth!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי עֶשְׂרִין וְחַד נְכֵי דַּנְקָא הָוֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's formula of 25 minus a sixth

steps.title: First correction: remove a sixth and also a זוז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises the formula: subtract a sixth and then one more זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, take away a sixth and a זוז, and these are for פדיון הבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to fix the formula by also subtracting one extra זוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the first result was too high by almost a whole זוז, the גמרא adds the removal of one זוז. This attempt keeps the original order: the sixth comes off first, then the זוז.

phrases.english: Rather, take away a sixth and a zuz,
and these are for the redemption of the son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by adjusting the formula
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Subtracting only a sixth is enough
steps.terutzMaskana: Subtract a sixth and an additional זוז

steps.title: Still not exact: now it is too little
steps.stepSummary: Subtracting a sixth and then a זוז leaves 19⅚, which is twenty less a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is still twenty less a sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the new formula and finds it now comes out slightly too low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 20⅚ minus 1 equals 19⅚. That is "20 minus one דנקא," so it falls a sixth short of the required twenty.

phrases.english: It is still twenty less a sixth!

steps.kashyaTarget: The formula of a sixth and then a זוז

steps.title: Final correction: first a זוז, then a sixth
steps.stepSummary: Subtract one זוז first, leaving 24, then subtract a sixth of 24, which is 4. Exactly twenty remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, take away a זוז and then a sixth, and these are for פדיון הבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reverses the order of subtraction, and the result is exactly twenty זוזים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the order changes the answer. 25 − 1 = 24, and a sixth of 24 is exactly 4. 24 − 4 = 20, which is precisely five סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: A זוז and (then) a sixth — note the reversed order

steps.confusionAlert: The words look almost the same as step 3. The only change is the order: "שתותא וזוזא" (sixth first) versus "זוזא ושתותא" (zuz first). That order is the whole point, because a sixth of 24 is not the same as a sixth of 25.
steps.whatToRemember: The correct method is 25 minus 1 = 24, then minus a sixth (4) = 20 זוזים = five סלעים for פדיון הבן.

phrases.english: Rather, take away a zuz and a sixth,
phrases.notes: Take off the one זוז first, then a sixth of the 24 that are left.

phrases.english: and these are for the redemption of the son,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by reversing the order of subtraction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Subtract the sixth before the זוז
steps.terutzMaskana: Subtract the זוז first, then a sixth, giving exactly 20

steps.title: The result expressed in מתקלי
steps.stepSummary: The twenty זוזים equal twenty מתקלי by weight, which are worth twenty-eight and a half זוזים plus half a דנקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For these amount to twenty מתקלי in the weight of the דינר called מתקלי, which are twenty-eight and a half זוזים and half a sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a note converting the פדיון הבן amount into another known coin standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line does not argue. It restates the final amount in a different local currency, the מתקלי. That way people who use that coin know how much to pay.

phrases.english: for they amount to twenty matkalei
by the weight of the dinar called matkalei,
which are twenty-eight zuz
and a half, and half a sixth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Converts the result of step 5 into another currency
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פדיון הבן amount equals 20 מתקלי, worth 28½ זוזים and half a דנקא.

steps.title: רבא: the biblical סלע is three and a third דינרים
steps.stepSummary: רבא claims that the סלע of the Torah is worth only three and a third דינרים, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: the סלעים of the Torah are three and a third.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic and states that the biblical סלע is smaller than the familiar four-דינר סלע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now everyone assumed a סלע is four דינרים, so five סלעים equal twenty. רבא says the Torah's סלע is only 3⅓ דינרים. If he is right, the biblical amounts are smaller than people assumed. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The סלעים (שקלים) mentioned in the Torah

phrases.english: Rava says:
the Torah's selaim are three and a third (dinars),

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: סִילְעִים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא תְּלָתָא וְתִילְתָּא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New statement about the value of the biblical סלע

steps.title: רבא's proof from the פסוק, the תרגום, and a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A שקל is twenty גרה. The תרגום renders גרה as מעה. A ברייתא says six מעה make a דינר. So 20 ÷ 6 = 3⅓ דינרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "The שקל is twenty גרה," and we translate it "twenty מעין," and it is taught: six silver מעה are a דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his claim by linking three sources together into a calculation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works in three steps. The פסוק says a שקל is twenty גרה. The תרגום tells us a גרה is a מעה. The ברייתא says six מעה equal one דינר. Twenty מעה divided by six gives 3⅓ דינרים.

keyTerms.meaning: A small biblical unit of weight/money
And we translate (in the Aramaic תרגום)
A small silver coin, a sixth of a דינר

phrases.english: as it is written: "The shekel is twenty gera,"
and we translate: "twenty ma'in,"
and it is taught: six silver ma'ah are a dinar.

steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות ל:יג with the תרגום, and a ברייתא that six מעה equal a דינר

steps.title: Challenge: a סלע of הקדש has forty-eight פונדיונין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the סלע of הקדש has forty-eight פונדיונין, which is twenty-four מעה, or four דינרים. That contradicts רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: But the סלע of הקדש is forty-eight פונדיונין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רבא's claim about the size of the סלע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פונדיון is half a מעה, so forty-eight פונדיונין equal twenty-four מעה. Since six מעה make a דינר, twenty-four מעה equal four דינרים. That is a full four-דינר סלע, not the 3⅓ that רבא claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: Small coins, each half a מעה

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
But is not the sela of the Sanctuary
forty-eight pundeyonin?
phrases.notes: 48 פונדיונין make 24 מעה, which is 4 דינרים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: וַהֲלֹא סֶלַע שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנֶה פּוּנְדְּיוֹנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's statement and proof in steps 7 and 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the biblical סלע is 3⅓ דינרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 48 פונדיונין = 24 מעה = 4 דינרים, so the holy סלע is four דינרים

steps.title: The ברייתא explains what the extra פונדיון is for
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quoted in the challenge ends by explaining that an extra פונדיון is a fee for changing a large coin into small coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this extra פונדיון for? It is a fee for changing the coin into small change!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the challenge. The ברייתא explains that the extra פונדיון is a money-changer's fee and not part of the סלע itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about redeeming a consecrated field. There the חכמים require a סלע and a פונדיון for each year, which over 49 years comes to 49 סלעים plus 49 פונדיונין. Since a סלע is 48 פונדיונין, that equals 50 סלעים plus one extra פונדיון, and the ברייתא explains that this extra coin is an exchange fee. Either way, the ברייתא assumes a סלע of 48 פונדיונין (24 מעה, four דינרים), so the challenge against רבא's three and a third still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin, worth half a מָעָה
An exchange fee or premium paid to a money-changer
Breaking a large coin into small change

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count the extra פונדיון as part of the סלע. It is only a service fee, so the סלע itself is still 48 פונדיונין.

phrases.english: This pundeyon, what is its function?
phrases.notes: Refers to the extra coin mentioned in the ברייתא

phrases.english: It is a premium for exchanging into small coins!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 9, which keeps the contradiction to רבא in force
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the Torah's סלע is three and a third דינרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the extra coin is set aside as a fee, the סלע is exactly 48 פונדיונין, which is four דינרים, not three and a third.

steps.title: The ברייתא describes the time after the coins were increased
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's four דינרים refers to the period after the חכמים added one-sixth to the סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא speaks of the time after they added to the coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It says the ברייתא is describing the סלע after the חכמים made it bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's original סלע was 20 מעה, which is three and a third דינרים, just as רבא said. Later the חכמים added one-sixth, which is 4 more מעה, making 24 מעה, or four דינרים. So רבא and the ברייתא are each talking about a different time period.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of them, meaning onto the coins

steps.whyThisMatters: This one-sixth addition explains why later halachic amounts for פדיון הבן and similar payments are higher than the original Torah values.

phrases.english: After they added onto them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 9 and 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different time periods: before and after the rabbinic addition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's four דינרים contradicts רבא's three and a third
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא describes the original Torah סלע. The ברייתא describes the enlarged סלע after the one-sixth addition.

steps.title: A source showing the שקל may be increased but not decreased
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוקים that the שקל is 20 גרה. The word 'יהיה' allows adding to it, and the word 'הוא' forbids reducing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Twenty גרה shall be the שקל.' We learn that the שקל is twenty גרה. And how do we know that if they wish to add, they may add? The פסוק says 'shall be.' Might they also reduce it? The פסוק says 'it is.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the חכמים were allowed to increase the שקל. This backs up the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יהיה' ('shall be') points to the future, which teaches that the amount can change upward. The word 'הוא' ('it is') fixes a minimum, so the שקל can never be less than 20 גרה. This proves the one-sixth addition was legitimate.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah unit of value, equal to a מָעָה
'Shall be', the word that allows an increase
'It is', the word that blocks any reduction

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'Twenty gera shall be the shekel' —
we learn regarding the shekel that it is twenty gera,
and from where do we know that if one wants to add, he may add?
The verse states: 'shall be',
One might think he may reduce it?
The verse states: 'it is'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 11 with a source
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים were allowed to add to the Torah's שקל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'יהיה' and 'הוא' in the פסוקים about the שקל
steps.whatToRemember: The Torah's סלע is 20 מעה, which is three and a third דינרים. The חכמים may increase it, and they added one-sixth to make 24 מעה, which is four דינרים. It may never go below 20.

steps.title: רב אשי asks for change from his redemption money
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי sent seventeen זוזים for פדיון הבן and asked for back the extra third of a זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי sent seventeen זוזים to רב אחא son of רבינא for the redemption of a firstborn son. He sent him a message: 'Let the master send me back the extra third that is in this money.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about paying for פדיון הבן. רב אשי works from רבא's value of the Torah's סלע and asks for change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פדיון הבן costs five סלעים. If each סלע is three and a third דינרים, five come to sixteen and two-thirds. רב אשי sent seventeen, so he asked for the extra third back.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeeming a firstborn son from a כֹּהֵן for five סְלָעִים

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי שַׁדַּר לֵיהּ שִׁבְסַר זוּזֵי
phrases.english: Rav Ashi sent seventeen zuz
to Rav Aḥa son of Ravina
for the redemption of the firstborn son,
he sent him a message: Let the Master send me
the extra third that is in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי שַׁדַּר לֵיהּ שִׁבְסַר זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבא's value of the סלע in a real case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using the Torah's סלע of three and a third דינרים, five סלעים come to sixteen and two-thirds.

steps.title: רב אחא replies that three more זוזים are owed
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא answered that, because of the added one-sixth, רב אשי actually owed three more זוזים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back: 'Let the master send me three more, because of what they added to the coins!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא turns down רב אשי's request. He points out that the rabbinic addition makes the payment larger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the addition, each סלע is four דינרים, so five סלעים are twenty. רב אשי sent seventeen, so he was three short, not a third over. The story puts both of the גמרא's points into practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a respectful way of saying 'you'

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, פדיון הבן follows the increased סלע: five סלעים are twenty דינרים.

phrases.english: He sent him back: Let the Master send me
three more that they added onto them!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: לְשַׁדַּר לִי מָר תְּלָתָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the request in step 13 based on the addition from step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's request for a third of a זוז back
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He ignored the rabbinic one-sixth addition, which raises the total to twenty

steps.title: רבי חנינא: what unspecified 'silver' means in each part of תנ"ך
steps.stepSummary: An unspecified 'silver' means a סלע in the Torah, a ליטרא in נביאים, and a קינטר in כתובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Every 'silver' mentioned in the Torah without detail means a סלע. In the נביאים it means a ליטרא. In the כתובים it means a קינטר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching about coins. רבי חנינא explains how big an amount of 'silver' is when the פסוק does not say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'silver' means a bigger unit depending on which part of תנ"ך it appears in. A ליטרא is 25 סלעים, and a קינטר is 100 סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Writings, the third section of תנ"ך

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל כֶּסֶף הָאָמוּר בַּתּוֹרָה סְתָם — סֶלַע,
phrases.english: any silver stated in the Torah without specification is a sela,
of the Prophets: litras,
of the Writings: centenaria,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: כׇּל כֶּסֶף הָאָמוּר בַּתּוֹרָה סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on coin values, related in theme only
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unspecified silver means a סלע in the Torah, a ליטרא in נביאים, and a קינטר in כתובים.

steps.title: The exception: עפרון's silver was in large units
steps.stepSummary: The silver אברהם paid עפרון was in קינטרין even though it appears in the Torah, because 'accepted by the merchant' means a currency accepted everywhere, and some places call a קינטר a 'שקל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for the silver of עפרון. Even though it is written in the Torah without detail, it was קינטרין, as it says, 'Four hundred שקל of silver, accepted by the merchant.' And there is a place where they call a קינטר a 'תיקלא' (שקל).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives one exception to his rule, along with a proof. The 400 שקלים paid to עפרון were huge units, not ordinary סלעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עובר לסוחר' show the money was accepted as 'שקלים' everywhere, including in places where 'שקל' means a קינטר. So each of the 400 was worth 100 סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who sold מְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה to אַבְרָהָם
Accepted by the merchant, meaning currency good everywhere

steps.confusionAlert: This is an exception within רבי חנינא's rule, not a rejection of it. Unspecified Torah silver is still a סלע everywhere else.

phrases.english: except for the silver of Ephron,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה סְתָם — קִינְטָרִין,
phrases.english: for even though it is written in the Torah without specification, it is centenaria,
as it is written: 'Four hundred shekels of silver,
current money with the merchant',
and there is a place
where they call a centenarius a 'shekel'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exception to רבי חנינא's rule in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עפרון's 400 שקלים were קינטרין, because 'עובר לסוחר' means a currency accepted everywhere, including where a קינטר is called a שקל.
steps.whatToRemember: Unspecified silver is a סלע in the Torah, a ליטרא in נביאים, and a קינטר in כתובים. The one exception is עפרון's silver, which was קינטרין even though it is in the Torah.

steps.title: The חכמים almost put away all the world's silver and gold
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא reports that the חכמים wanted to put away all silver and gold, because it might be holy metal from ירושלים. A verse then showed it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: The חכמים wanted to put away all the silver and gold in the world because of the silver and gold of ירושלים. They did so until they found a פסוק showing that it is permitted, as it says: 'And robbers will enter it and make it ordinary.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא tells us the חכמים almost banned using any silver or gold at all. Their worry was that it might be holy metal from the בית המקדש that the enemies took.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear was that holy metal (הקדש) from the Temple treasury had gotten mixed into all the world's silver and gold. The verse says robbers 'made it ordinary' (חללוה). This teaches that once the enemies plundered it, its holiness was gone, so using it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: to put away / hide away so no one uses it
the silver and gold of ירושלים (the Temple treasure)
and they made it ordinary (took away its holiness)

steps.confusionAlert: The verse is really from יחזקאל, not the חמשה חומשי תורה. Here ״מן התורה״ is used loosely to mean 'from Scripture.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the principle that Temple property seized by robbers loses its holiness. That principle is what allows these coins to be used.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּיקְּשׁוּ לִגְנוֹז כׇּל כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
phrases.english: They (the Sages) wanted to put away all the silver and gold in the world
because of the silver and gold of Jerusalem,
phrases.notes: The Temple treasure that enemies took and mixed into other metal.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁמָּצְאוּ לוֹ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: until they found for it a verse from Scripture
showing that it is permitted,
as it is said: 'And robbers will enter it and make it ordinary.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about whether metal that might come from the Temple may be used. It ties back to the worn דינרים mentioned earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Silver and gold that may come from ירושלים's holy treasure is permitted, because robbers' plunder made it ordinary.

steps.title: Is ירושלים most of the world?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא: why would the חכמים forbid all the world's metal because of ירושלים, when ירושלים is only a tiny part of the world?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is ירושלים the majority of the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a sharp question against רבי אושעיא's version. It does not make sense that the חכמים would worry about all the metal everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a normal rule that we follow the majority (רוב). Most silver and gold in the world never came from ירושלים, so it should be permitted anyway. The חכמים would never have needed to think about banning all of it.

phrases.english: But is Jerusalem the majority of the world?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wide scope of רבי אושעיא's statement in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's claim that the חכמים wanted to put away all silver and gold in the world.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ירושלים's metal is a tiny minority of the world's metal. By the rule of majority, the world's silver and gold should never have been suspect.

steps.title: אביי narrows it to the worn coins of הדריינוס and טריינוס
steps.stepSummary: אביי revises the statement. The חכמים only wanted to put away the worn דינרים of הדריינוס and טריינוס, because those coins were made from ירושלים's coins. The same verse permits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: The חכמים wanted to put away the worn-out דינרים of הדריינוס and טריינוס because of the coins of ירושלים. They did so until they found a פסוק showing that it is permitted, as it says: 'And robbers will enter it and make it ordinary.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי fixes the problem by making the worry much smaller. It was not about all the world's metal, only about specific Roman coins that were heavily made from Temple metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kings הדריינוס and טריינוס minted their coins using metal from ירושלים's treasure. So in those coins, holy metal could be a large part, and the majority rule does not solve the problem. Still, the verse ״וחללוה״ teaches that the plundered metal lost its holiness, so these coins are permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: the דינר coins of the emperors הדריינוס and טריינוס

steps.whatToRemember: The concern was only about the worn coins of הדריינוס and טריינוס, not all metal in the world. They are permitted, because robbers who plunder Temple property make it ordinary (״ובאו בה פריצים וחללוה״).
steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not disagree with the verse or the final ruling. He only changes WHAT the חכמים were worried about.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּקְּשׁוּ לִגְנוֹז דִּינָרָא הַדְרִיָּינָא טִירְיָיאנָא שְׁיָיאפָא,
phrases.english: They wanted to put away the worn-out dinars of Hadrian and Trajan,
because of the coins of Jerusalem,
phrases.notes: These coins were made with a lot of Temple metal.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁמָּצְאוּ לָהּ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: until they found for it a verse from Scripture
showing that it is permitted,
as it is said: 'And robbers will enter it and make it ordinary.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by reformulating רבי אושעיא's statement more narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry was about all silver and gold in the world, which makes no sense because of the majority rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry was only about the worn coins of הדריינוס and טריינוס, which contain much Temple metal. Even those are permitted by the verse.
